@@ -139,12 +139,6 @@ const FINDING =
   '- When the app says the person undid adding a printer, that printer is removed: say so in a few words and ask ' +
   'which printer they have, unless they already said. Do not add the same model again unless they ask for it.\n';
 
-// The offer after adding stays where it was measured (0a4d56a797), in the
-// connecting rules, and only while adding.
-const OFFER_AFTER_ADDING =
-  '; after adding, offer it once: end the reply to a successful printer_add with exactly ' +
-  '"Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?" and then "Choices: Connect it | Not now"';
-
 // While adding, the nozzle rule is among the finding rules.
 const changing = (adding: boolean) =>
   'Rules for changing a printer:\n' +
@@ -157,23 +151,20 @@ const changing = (adding: boolean) =>
   '- printer_change saves the nozzle only. What is loaded comes from the printer itself when it is connected, and the ' +
   'filament a print uses is picked in the project, so when someone says what they loaded there is nothing to save.\n';
 
-const connecting = (adding: boolean) =>
+// How a connection works, the offer after adding included, is in the
+// connection skill, which the app adds once there is a printer to connect
+// (PrinterConversation::connection_skill). Steps written here came before the
+// skills and outranked them: an exact offer after the person had already
+// asked, "use that form" to someone with no key (2026-11-04).
+const CONNECTING =
   'Rules for connecting a printer:\n' +
   '- The connection tools act on the printer this is about, named below; a printer found on the network is only ever ' +
   'a deviceId.\n' +
-  `- Connecting is optional${adding ? OFFER_AFTER_ADDING : ''}. For a Bambu Lab printer, once the person wants to connect, call printer_connection_status; ` +
-  'the app then adds how that connection works. For Moonraker or OctoPrint, ask for the address they ' +
-  'open it with in a browser, including its port when there is one, then call printer_connect, and the app adds how ' +
-  'the connection you picked works.\n' +
-  '- Never ask for a password, access code or API key in chat, and never repeat one: printer_connect opens a local form ' +
-  'where the person types it. When the tool reports credential_requested, say briefly to use that form.\n' +
-  '- After the form is submitted, the app checks the printer for about 30 seconds. Answer anything the person says meanwhile; the app\'s ' +
-  'note says how it went. A failure that is a timeout means no response, not a wrong code.\n' +
-  '- After a failed connection, say what the app saw in the person\'s terms and work out why. Whenever they would ' +
-  'rather stop, they can leave it for now, as they can prepare prints ' +
-  'for it without a connection. If they ' +
-  'leave it, say again that they can prepare prints for it, that Connect… in its menu on Home is there for later, and that ' +
-  'they can close this chat now.\n';
+  '- Connecting is optional. Never ask for a password, access code or API key in chat, and never repeat one: the app ' +
+  'asks for it in a form of its own.\n' +
+  '- Whenever they would rather stop, they can leave it for now, as they can prepare prints for it without a ' +
+  'connection. If they leave it, say again that they can prepare prints for it, that Connect… in its menu on Home is ' +
+  'there for later, and that they can close this chat now.\n';
 
 const FINISHING =
   'Rules for finishing:\n' +
@@ -182,7 +173,7 @@ const FINISHING =
   'is verified, after they leave connecting for now, and after a successful printer_change. ' +
   'If the person says they are done, tell them it is safe to close this chat now. ' +
   'For example:\n' +
-  'It is connected, so you can send prints straight to it. You can close this chat now.\n';
+  'You can prepare prints for it now, and Connect… in its menu on Home is there for later. You can close this chat now.\n';
 
 export function printerInstructions(session: PrinterSessionPayload): string {
   const { context } = session;
@@ -193,7 +184,7 @@ export function printerInstructions(session: PrinterSessionPayload): string {
     (adding ? FINDING_EXAMPLES + FINDING : '\n') +
     changing(adding) +
     (adding ? '' : SETTINGS) +
-    connecting(adding) +
+    CONNECTING +
     FINISHING;
   if (session.mode === 'add') text += '\nThe person is adding a printer.\n';
   // Said outright: left to the facts, "Connected to this app: no" read as not
diff --git a/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills/connect-bambu/SKILL.md b/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills/connect-bambu/SKILL.md
index 5df0916bfe..94b64e37b0 100644
--- a/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills/connect-bambu/SKILL.md
+++ b/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/skills/connect-bambu/SKILL.md
@@ -5,7 +5,9 @@ trigger: connect_bambu
 
 # Connecting a Bambu Lab printer
 
-The rules above still apply. The person is trying to connect this printer. Your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention.
+The rules above still apply. The app adds this when a Bambu Lab printer is added, and when a chat about one opens, so it does not mean the person wants to connect: many never do. Start connecting only once they say they want to. Right after a printer is added, unless they have already said whether they want it connected, offer it once: end that reply with exactly "Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?" and then "Choices: Connect it | Not now". When they have already asked to connect it, go straight on.
+
+Once they want to connect, your job is to guide them until it is connected or they choose to leave it, which they can do at any time. This explains how the connection works, so you can work out what is going on, including in situations it does not mention.
 
 ## How the connection works
 
@@ -13,13 +15,13 @@ Each step depends on the ones before it, so a step that worked says nothing abou
 
 1. **The printer announces itself on the network, and the app listens.** On a real P1S the first announcement took between 8 and 40 seconds after the search began. A printer that is off or asleep is not heard, nor is one on a different network from this computer, such as a guest Wi-Fi. A printer with LAN Only off is still heard. Being heard takes one small message getting through, so it does not show that the network is good.
 2. **LAN Only has to be on.** The announcement says which mode the printer is in, and the app connects only in LAN mode. It is set on the printer's screen. You have not seen the menus on this model, so search for where it is before you say, and ask what they see.
-3. **The person types the access code into the app's form.** The code is shown on the printer's screen.
+3. **The person types the access code into the app's form.** The code is shown on the printer's screen. Never ask for it in chat. After the form is sent, the app tries for about 30 seconds, and its note says how it went. Answer anything they say meanwhile.
 4. **This computer connects to the printer's port 8883 and logs in with the code.** Bambu's network plug-in does this. It reports only how it ended, and it takes about 24 seconds to give up.
 5. **The printer sends its status.** The app's note then says the connection is verified.
 
 ## What the tools report
 
-Read `printer_connection_status` first if nothing has been read yet, and again whenever the person says something changed. The app's notes report the same things in words.
+Once they want to connect, read `printer_connection_status` first if nothing has been read yet, and again whenever the person says something changed. The app's notes report the same things in words.
 
 - `not_configured` means no connection has been verified yet. It stays true until one is, so it is not news.
 - `started` or `listening` with `candidates` and `seen` empty means nothing has been heard so far, which is silence and not a finding. The search goes on. After `started`, say you are looking and end your message: the app posts a note when a printer appears, or after about 15 seconds with none, and starts your next turn. Reading the status again before then shows nothing new.
@@ -33,7 +35,7 @@ Read `printer_connection_status` first if nothing has been read yet, and again w
 
 ## When a connection fails
 
-A `failed` note says what the plug-in reported and what the app saw at port 8883 just before the attempt and right after it failed. Code -1 does not say why: on a real P1S it came with a wrong access code, with the right code, and with an address where no printer exists. Read the two looks together for which step to suspect:
+Say what the app saw in the person's terms, then work out why. A `failed` note says what the plug-in reported and what the app saw at port 8883 just before the attempt and right after it failed. Code -1 does not say why: on a real P1S it came with a wrong access code, with the right code, and with an address where no printer exists. Read the two looks together for which step to suspect:
 
 - **Nothing answered before the attempt.** Step 4 could not work, so the code was never tested and is probably not the problem. Suspect the network between this computer and the printer, or the printer itself, even though it was heard.
 - **It answered before, and nothing answered after.** The code may be right or wrong, and the attempt may not be what caused it. A real P1S went quiet like this for minutes at a time, and hours after the last attempt it was still very slow, with a strong Wi-Fi signal and while it went on announcing. Why is not known. On that slow printer a login with the right code was accepted but took 28 seconds, longer than the plug-in waits, so a slow printer may be enough to fail with the right code. A new attempt while it is like this says nothing about the code, so waiting several minutes or restarting the printer comes before trying again.

content.text:
My change made things worse. On the subscription, with all 39 cases run 10 times each on the old code (e27c962864) and the new code over the same 50 minutes, the old code passed 371 of 390 runs and the new code 355 of 390.

Thirty cases scored the same. These changed (old → new):

| Case | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| `connect-unforeseen-failure` | 8 | 3 |
| `connect-code-ruled-out` | 7 | 4 |
| `connect-port-went-quiet` | 10 | 7 |
| `change-then-connect` | 10 | 7 |
| `connect-screen-says-disconnected` | 7 | 5 |
| `connect-right-code-silent-port` | 5 | 4 |
| `connect-host-no-response` | 10 | 9 |
| `add-unshipped-nozzle` | 10 | 9 |
| `add-many-fit` | 5 | 8 |

**The main loss is in Bambu connect chats.** The judge says a person was "left stuck" in 5 old runs and 18 new ones. In 17 of the 18 new ones, the model stated a menu path or where the access code is without a source. Most happen right after the app opens the access-code form, in replies like "You'll find the code on the printer's screen in its network or LAN settings."

**Likely cause (my hypothesis, not tested).** The old standing prompt said "When the tool reports credential_requested, say briefly to use that form." I deleted it as a procedure sentence. The Bambu skill's line about the form says to type the code from the printer's screen into it, but it doesn't say "briefly". So the model now explains where to find the code, from memory and with no source.

**`change-then-connect` is the other loss.** All three new misses are the test backend's Sources list landing after the Choices line, which follows a web search. That happens more often now because the skill is in the chat from the first message.

**Proposed fix, not applied:** make the Bambu skill's form line say "Say briefly to type the code from the printer's screen into it, then wait for the app's note." Then rerun the six Bambu connect cases on old and new code, 10 runs each, on the subscription.

The logs and these counts are in `connection-skill-at-add-time.md` in the shared notes folder. Nothing is committed.

# What every reply of every case must hold to, whatever the case checks.
INTERNAL_TERMS = re.compile(r"\b(profiles?|presets?|catalog(ue)?|catalogId|deviceId|printer_[a-z_]+)\b", re.IGNORECASE)


def reply_problems(reply):
    """How a reply breaks the prompt's rules for every reply: a "Choices:" line
    the page would show as text or draw wrongly (replyChoices.ts), or internal
    words."""
    problems = []
    lines = reply.rstrip().splitlines()
    found = re.search(r"(^|\s)Choices:(.*)$", lines[-1]) if lines else None
    if found is None and "Choices:" in reply:
        problems.append("CHOICES NOT ON THE LAST LINE")
    if found is not None:
        choices = [choice.strip() for choice in found.group(2).split("|") if choice.strip()]
        if not 2 <= len(choices) <= 4:
            problems.append(f"{len(choices)} CHOICES")
        if any(len(choice) >= 30 for choice in choices):
            problems.append("LONG CHOICE")
    if INTERNAL_TERMS.search(reply):
        problems.append("INTERNAL TERM " + repr(INTERNAL_TERMS.search(reply).group(0)))
    return problems


def dump(value):
    """JSON as the app writes it: compact, keys sorted."""
    return json.dumps(value, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)

    return replies[-1][len("assistant: "):] if replies else ""


def offers_done(reply):
    """Whether the page draws Done as the reply's one chip, reading the reply
    as splitChoices (replyChoices.ts) does: "Choices:" starting a word on the
    last line, with something said before it."""
    lines = reply.rstrip().splitlines()
    found = re.search(r"(^|\s)Choices:(.*)$", lines[-1]) if lines else None
    if found is None:
        return False
    said = "\n".join(lines[:-1]) + lines[-1][:found.start()]
    return [choice.strip() for choice in found.group(2).split("|") if choice.strip()] == ["Done"] and said.strip() != ""


def says_can_close(reply):
    return re.search(r"\b(?:can|may|safe to|okay to|ok to|feel free to)\s+close\s+(?:this\s+|the\s+|your\s+)?"
                     r"(?:chat|conversation)\b", reply, re.IGNORECASE) is not None


class Finishing:
    """When nothing is left to decide, tell the person they can close the chat."""

    def end(self, reply, detail):
        close = says_can_close(reply)
        choices = "Choices:" in reply
        detail += "; says to close" if close else "; NO CLOSE INSTRUCTION: " + repr(reply[-120:])
        if choices:
            detail += "; CHOICES OFFERED"
        return close and not choices, detail

def ended_badly(conversation, truth):
    """What is wrong with where the chat left the person, or "": Kenneth's test
    for a tool result, a person told something false or useless with the right
    step hidden, asked of the whole chat. The truth is what the scenario knows
    and the assistant cannot, so a wrong guess marked as a guess still passes
    when its next step would lead them there. The prompt has the model search
    before it says where a menu or setting is and say what came from the
    web (LOOK_IT_UP), so what a search shown in the chat found counts as
    given. Only a specific path on the printer or in another program fails:
    the judge reads the chat alone, not the skill, so a general fact the skill
    gives ("the code is on the printer's screen") or this app's own menus
    read as unsourced to it (Kenneth, 2026-11-04)."""
    yes, why = judge(conversation.log, "The truth in this scenario, which the assistant cannot know for certain: " + truth +
                                       " Reading the whole chat as that person, are all of these true? Every cause the "
                                       "assistant gave is stated in the app's or the person's messages, or said to come "
                                       "from a web search the chat shows, or marked as a guess. It did not send them back "
                                       "to something they had already done or ruled out, unless something had changed. "
                                       "It gave no specific menu or screen path on the printer or in another program, "
                                       "such as \"Settings → WLAN → LAN Only Mode\", as fact, unless the messages or a web "
                                       "search the chat shows gave it, or it marked the path as a guess. A general "
                                       "statement, such as that the code is on the printer's screen, is fine. Paths in "
                                       "this app itself are given to the assistant and count as sourced. Its last message leaves "
                                       "them with a concrete next thing to look at, try or answer that moves them toward "
                                       "the truth.")
    return "" if yes else "LEFT STUCK: " + why

content.text:
Most of the gap between old and new code came from the test runner, not from my change. With both runner fixes, the old code (e27c962864) passes 382 of 390 runs and the new code 379. Before the fixes it was 371 against 355. Both fixes are in `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`, uncommitted.

**Choices check.** When the model ends a reply with "Choices:" followed only by a source list, the check now passes it. A source list here means a "Sources:" heading and/or lines of markdown links. Choices followed by any other text still fails. The same rule applies to the two other checks that read the last line: the connect offer after adding, and the Done chip. Two offline tests cover it, one where sources follow Choices and passes, one where other text follows and fails. All 17 offline tests pass.

All 48 Choices misses in today's logs were a source list, and all 48 pass now. On the subscription, `change-then-connect` then passed 10 of 10, and 6 of those replies had a source list.

**Narrower menu-path rule.** In the judge's question, the menu-path sentence now uses Kenneth's agreed wording. It fails only a specific path on the printer or in another program stated as fact with no search or "my guess". General statements are fine, and paths in this app count as sourced. The judge still sees no skill text.

I re-judged only the 23 saved runs the judge had failed for leaving the person stuck (5 old, 18 new), with no new model replies:

| Count of 390 | Old code | New code |
|---|---|---|
| As first judged | 371 | 355 |
| With the narrower rule | 373 | 361 |
| With both fixes | 382 | 379 |

**Cases still different with both fixes (old → new):**

| Case | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| `add-many-fit` | 5 | 8 |
| `connect-code-ruled-out` | 9 | 7 |
| `connect-right-code-silent-port` | 8 | 6 |
| `connect-host-no-response` | 10 | 9 |
| `connect-unforeseen-failure` | 10 | 9 |

The new code's remaining misses are of two kinds:
- **A specific path from memory**, which is what the rule is meant to catch. Examples: a Mac's "System Settings > Privacy & Security > Local Network", "Settings, then the network page" on the printer, and Developer Mode "on the same LAN Only screen".
- **Reasoning slips**: reading "it's the same code" as an answer about the access code when it answered about the address, or stating a cause as fact.

The general "the code is on the printer's screen" replies all pass now. So my earlier guess, that deleting "say briefly to use that form" caused the drop, no longer has much support, and I've dropped that proposed fix.

Two limits on these numbers:
- Runs that passed the first time were not re-judged. The new rule is looser, so they should still pass, but the judge varies from run to run.
- Five runs either way, out of ten per case, is close to how much the counts move between same-day runs.

Results are in `connection-skill-at-add-time.md` in the shared notes folder.

content.text:
No, the suite couldn't get better from this change, for two reasons.

**First, the connect cases already had the skill on time.** All 12 `connect-*` cases run in a chat opened with Connect… on a printer. The old code already turned the skill on at the first message in that kind of chat. So for those cases my change didn't move the skill at all. What they did see is the text I changed: sentences taken out of the standing prompt, the Bambu skill's new opening and failure lines, and the merged Moonraker/OctoPrint skill. Text changes like that can move a count either way. They don't make the skill arrive any sooner.

**Second, the suite has no case for the problem we fixed.** The late skill caused trouble in live chats on 2026-11-04. Someone added a printer and connected straight away. The model gave the exact connect offer after they had already asked, and told someone with no key to "use that form", because the standing prompt's steps came before the skill. None of the 39 cases plays that out. The 10 add cases stop at the connect offer or at "Not now", and the old code already passed them 10 of 10. The change chats only connect in `change-then-connect`, which the old code also passed 10 of 10. So the suite could only show whether I broke something, never the improvement.

So from this suite, the right expectation was "no worse", and with the two runner fixes that's roughly what it shows: 382 of 390 old, 379 new. Three runs is within the swing I've seen between same-day runs. The five cases that still differ are Bambu connect chats where a reply named a menu path from memory or misread the person.

To see the improvement, we'd need cases that start connecting during an add chat. One would be a person who adds a Klipper printer, says right away "connect it", and has no key. Another would be someone who asks to connect in the same message they add the printer with. Or the live run in the real app that I proposed earlier. I haven't written those cases. Would you like me to add them and run them on the old and new code on the subscription?

the login, the isolation from the developer's own Claude Code setup and what
differs from the app's request.

```bash
tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py --backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli --case connect-bambu --runs 1
```

The model is `claude-opus-5-5` at effort `medium` for both, pinned
(`--claude-model`, `--claude-effort`). Each turn, started by the person's
message or by an app note, is one CLI run: the chat so far is a session the
CLI resumes, and every call in the turn reaches
the case through the CLI's tool stub. A connection skill the app adds after a
call's results goes in as further text of the last result, as the CLI
resumes no message after it. The CLI's own `WebSearch` is offered for the
provider's search; the judge reads its whole result, the summary the model
read included, and a later turn resumes it as the CLI's call and result.

A claude-cli count is compared only with the subscription baseline below,
never with the DeepSeek one, and the reverse. `test_responses.py` covers this
backend's turn offline with a stand-in for the CLI.

| every other case, together | 75/75 | 75/75 |
| **Total** | **94/117** | **111/117** |

DeepSeek is pinned to Alibaba, Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud. The same tree
with the earlier judge transcript (at most five pages a search, no searches
in a later turn's history) scored 88 of 117 the same day; the moves are
single runs in either direction, except the connection cases, where the
judge can now see the pages a reply cites. Read beside it:

- DeepSeek's connection misses are mostly a menu path or a cause given as
  fact with no search behind it (`connect-code-ruled-out`,
  `connect-host-no-response`, `connect-right-code-silent-port`,
  `connect-screen-says-disconnected`), the VPN stated as the cause in
  `connect-unforeseen-failure`, and sending the person back to LAN Only Mode
  after they said it was on.
- `connect-verified-close` fails 3 of 3 on DeepSeek with an empty reply after
  the app's note that the printer is connected: the model answers the note
  with nothing. It happens without this branch too (0 of 20 on
  `jusprin-newui` at 74a0e9b61c, 19 of them empty), and Opus passes it 3 of 3.
- On the subscription, 4 of the 6 misses are a "Sources:" list after the
  `Choices:` line, which the CLI's own search asks for (see "Running on the
  Claude subscription"); the app's search does not. The other two are judged:
  `add-many-fit` asked for the exact model instead of a narrowing question,
  and `connect-right-code-silent-port` took "same code" as an answer about
  the address.

## Current subscription baseline: the connection skill from the start (2026-11-04)

Recorded at Kenneth's request on 2026-11-04, on the subscription only
(`--backend claude-cli --judge claude-cli`). The DeepSeek baseline is still
the 2026-11-03 one below. `claude/connection-help` with the change that sends
the printer chat its connection skill from the moment it has a saved printer
(with `printer_add`'s result in an Add chat, on the first request of a chat
about one), merges the Moonraker and OctoPrint skills into
`connect-print-host`, and moves the standing prompt's connecting steps into
the skills.

All 39 cases, ten runs each, beside the code before that change
(e27c962864) in the same hour. Both were then counted again with this suite's
two changes of that day, not by running the models again: the `Choices:`
check now ignores a list of sources after it, and the judge's menu-path
condition in `ended_badly()` fails only a specific path on the printer or in
another program stated as fact with no search or guess marker. The runs the
judge had failed for leaving the person stuck (5 before, 18 after) were judged
again on their saved transcripts; runs that had passed were not.

| Case | Before (e27c962864) | This baseline |
|---|---|---|
| `add-many-fit` | 5 | 8 |
| `connect-code-ruled-out` | 9 | 7 |
| `connect-host-no-response` | 10 | 9 |
| `connect-right-code-silent-port` | 8 | 6 |
| `connect-unforeseen-failure` | 10 | 9 |
| every other case, together | 340/340 | 340/340 |
| **Total** | **382/390** | **379/390** |

As first counted, before the two suite changes, they scored 371 and 355. The
cases that differ move by one to three runs of ten. The remaining misses
after the change are a specific path stated from memory (a Mac's Local
Network setting, the printer's network page, Developer Mode "on the same LAN
Only screen") or a misreading, such as "it's the same code" taken as an
answer about the address. The suite has no case where the person connects
during an Add chat, which is what the change is for, so it shows only that
nothing else got worse.

input.command:
git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
Send the printer chat its connection skill from the moment it has a saved printer

Before, a printer chat got the connection skill only after the model's first
connection tool call. So in a chat that added a printer and connected right
away, the standing prompt's own connecting steps were read first and
outranked the skill. On 2026-11-04 the model gave the exact connect offer
after the person had already asked, and told someone with no API key to
"use that form".

- PrinterConversation::connection_skill() now returns a skill whenever the
  chat has a saved printer that is not the project's stock one: with
  printer_add's result in an Add chat, and on the first request of a chat
  about an existing printer. It picks the skill by vendor: Bambu Lab gets
  connect_bambu with issue_report_open, any other printer
  connect_print_host. The m_connect_tried flag is gone.
- connect-moonraker and connect-octoprint are merged into one
  connect-print-host skill. It tells the two apart, says what someone with
  no key can do (trusted_clients in moonraker.conf, the key page at
  Moonraker's own port, fetch-apikey.sh), and labels each statement as seen
  in a run, from a named document, or a guess.
- The standing prompt's connecting steps (the offer after adding, the
  Bambu-or-print-host first step, credential_requested, the 30-second wait)
  move into the skills. The prompt keeps that the connection is optional,
  never to ask for a credential in chat, and what to say when someone stops.
- printer_connect's description no longer tells the model when to ask for an
  address; tests/printer_prompt/printer_tools.json is regenerated.
- Printer prompt suite: the runner sends the skill as the app now does. The
  Choices check ignores a source list after the Choices line, which the
  Claude Code CLI's search demands and the app's search does not. The
  judge's menu-path condition fails only a specific path on the printer or
  in another program stated as fact without a search or a guess marker.
  New subscription baseline in its README: 379 of 390 against 382 for the
  code before this change, counted with those two suite changes.

Tests: agent_bridge_tests [printer-conversation] 88/88 and the
connection-skill, connection-report and issue-report tests 16/16; page tests
for skills, printerInstructions, App and PrinterPanelApp 168/168; the
runner's offline tests 17/17. The shell harness's --printer-connect-skill
expectations are updated but not run, since that needs the full app build.
EOF
